record.original_question: Can one define anisotropic function spaces for ideal hydrodynamics that encode higher smoothness along flow lines, and prove existence and uniqueness of ideal fluid motion in those spaces in arbitrary dimension?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an ideal incompressible fluid on a Riemannian manifold $M$ of arbitrary dimension $n$, whose motion is governed by the incompressible Euler equations
$$\partial_t u + \nabla_u u = -\nabla p, \qquad \operatorname{div} u = 0,$$
with initial data $u_0$ tangent to $\partial M$ (if non-empty). Classical local well-posedness is known in isotropic Sobolev spaces $H^s$ with $s > n/2 + 1$ (Ebin–Marsden), where smoothness is required equally in all spatial directions.

Define a scale of anisotropic function spaces $\mathcal{A}^{s,k}(M)$ for divergence-free vector fields with the property that elements of $\mathcal{A}^{s,k}$ possess a baseline transverse regularity of order $s$ but additional regularity of order $k$ along the flow lines of the velocity field $u$ itself (so that directional derivatives $(u\cdot\nabla)^j u$ for $0 \le j \le k$ are controlled in the transverse space). Then prove existence and uniqueness of solutions to the incompressible Euler equations in these anisotropic spaces $\mathcal{A}^{s,k}(M)$, in arbitrary dimension $n \ge 2$, with regularity thresholds lower than those required by the isotropic theory.
artifact.category_tag: Anisotropic function spaces for Euler equations
artifact.status_search_result: No construction of anisotropic function spaces tailored to ideal hydrodynamics with the proposed flow-line regularity, together with a corresponding existence–uniqueness theorem in arbitrary dimension, appears in the literature. While anisotropic regularity conditions for Navier–Stokes and Lagrangian/flow-decoupling techniques exist, the problem of building such spaces and proving well-posedness of the Euler equations in them remains an open program.

status_evidence.title: Why global regularity for Navier–Stokes is hard
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of function-space approaches and difficulties for ideal/viscous incompressible flow well-posedness.
status_evidence.claim: Refined function-space frameworks for Euler/Navier–Stokes well-posedness remain a central open direction.

status_evidence.title: Existence and Smoothness of the Navier–Stokes Equation (Fefferman)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of open well-posedness questions for ideal and viscous incompressible flows.
status_evidence.claim: Well-posedness in refined spaces for incompressible flow is broadly open.
